evidence.description: The detached task returns filtered news items, then its array value is mapped using a closure that awaits MainActor.run.

candidates.explanation: The detached task returns an array, so mapping its value invokes synchronous Array.map. The closure contains an await and is therefore asynchronous, which cannot be passed to that API. The outer await does not make Array.map accept an asynchronous closure.
candidates.title: Asynchronous closure passed to synchronous Array.map

evidence.description: Initialization launches restoration in an unstructured task without waiting for it to complete.
The public load method independently starts a task that updates items and saves them.
After the detached file read, restoration replaces items with the cached result.

candidates.explanation: Initialization starts restoration without coordinating it with load. Restoration suspends while reading the file, allowing a load to update items in the meantime. When restoration resumes, it unconditionally replaces items with the cached snapshot, potentially discarding newly fetched news. MainActor isolation does not prevent this ordering problem across suspension points.
candidates.title: Background restoration can overwrite freshly loaded news

evidence.description: Each eligible load call starts a new task and invokes save, with no in-flight coordination.
Each save captures items and writes that snapshot to the shared file URL in a detached task.

candidates.explanation: Multiple load calls can overlap, and each save captures its own items snapshot before launching an independent detached write to the same file. An older snapshot can finish writing after a newer snapshot and overwrite it. Atomic writes protect against partial file replacement, but do not enforce snapshot ordering.
candidates.title: Concurrent saves can persist an outdated snapshot

evidence.description: Load returns no result, silently exits on decoding failure, and ignores thrown request errors.
Cache-reading and decoding errors are converted into an empty array.
Encoding and file-writing failures are caught and ignored.

candidates.explanation: Network, decoding, cache-reading, and persistence errors are suppressed without any error signal or diagnostic. In particular, a cache read or decoding failure is converted into an empty collection, while load returns synchronously and provides no completion result. Callers cannot distinguish these failures from successful operations that produce no change.
candidates.title: Operational failures are silently discarded
